Hi all — quick technical answers below (summarized). Happy to jump on the tech deep-dive.

1) Region pinning and backups:
- If you pin an account/workspace to the US, inference compute, model-serving instances, and primary data stores (request/response logs, model outputs) are served from US regions only.
- By default our managed backups are replicated asynchronously to a single geo-redundant replica for high durability; for US-pinned accounts the replica is also within the US (a different US region) — no EU/APAC replication occurs unless explicitly enabled.
- Option: For pilots we can disable cross-region replication entirely and keep backups in the primary US region only (this is a common request for regulated banks). We will need an operational runbook for DR if cross-region replication is disabled.

2) Cross-region failover behavior:
- Our standard failover uses same-geo failover within the pinned region first (e.g., us-west -> us-east). Only if there is a complete regional outage and a customer has opted into cross-region DR will we fail over to another geo (which we treat as an opt-in policy and document in the SLA).
- During failover, ephemeral caches and KV caches are rebuilt from persistent stores; request/response logs are never sent to another region unless cross-region DR is enabled.

3) Backups and PII:
- Backups contain serialized request/response records. We encrypt all backups at rest with customer keys (KMS/HSM integration available for Private deployments).
- PII handling: we offer a configuration to redact or pseudonymize sensitive fields before persistence (field-level redaction hooks or a prompt-layer preprocessor). We can enable pre-storage transformations for the pilot to strip or hash specified PII fields.

4) Retention & logging controls:
- Default retention: request/response logs = 30 days, admin/audit logs = 365 days.
- Configurable: we support per-account retention windows (min 7 days for request logs, max configurable up to 7 years subject to storage pricing and compliance needs).
- Audit logs are immutable for the retention window and exportable to customer S3/GCS for long-term archival.

5) Operational notes / next steps:
- If Acme requires zero cross-region replication, we'll enable US-only backups and provide an ops runbook + snapshot export cadence to your S3 for additional archival.
- We'll propose a pilot config: US region pinning + backups in US-only (no cross-region replication) + pre-storage PII pseudonymization for 90 days. After pilot, we can evaluate longer retention or opt-in DR.

Happy to join the call on Thu 4/9 to walk through the runbook and security controls.

—Aditya
